comments.author: @desthomas8747
comments.text: Colonel General von Moltke and Wilhelm II visit the Swiss Army, 1912. Colonel General Helmuth Johannes Ludwig von Moltke (right), also known as Moltke the Younger, Chief of the German General Staff from 1906 to 1914, visits manoeuvres of the Swiss Army with German Emperor Wilhelm II. General Moltke asked Swiss Commanding Officer how many troops he had,  150,000 all crack shots the Swiss General replied. Moltke asked what would they do if Germany invaded Switzerland with 300,000 troops. The Swiss General replied they would all fire twice then go home.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: That exchange has been retold for over a century, and it still captures how Switzerland thought about defence — deterrence by arithmetic rather than by size. For anyone who's read into the Swiss military history: does the reputation hold up, or has it been polished a little in the retelling?

comments.text: First chocolate was Fry from Bristol and second was be Cadbury - nestle a good 20 years later

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: Fry's bar in 1847 got there first, no argument — the Swiss claim is a narrower one: milk chocolate and conching, which arrived decades later and changed what the bar actually tasted like. The two stories tend to get told as though they're the same story.

replies.text: Switzerland has more of these chapters than one film can carry, and the Meili case and the suffrage timeline are two of the heaviest ones we didn't reach. We took the route we did deliberately, but there's a whole second film in what's left over.
